back: An increase in the percentage of a population living in urban areas.
An increase in the number of people living in towns, or in the area towns cover.
Movement of people out of large cities to smaller towns and rural areas, common in HICs.

front: Causes of rapid urban growth in LICs
back: Rural-urban migration (push and pull factors) plus high natural increase among young urban populations.
Drought, crop failure, land shortage, poverty, few jobs and services, conflict in rural areas.
Jobs, wages, schools, hospitals, piped water, electricity, family in town, perceived better life.
Since about 2007 over half the world's people are urban; growth is fastest in sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia.
Colonial controls limited African urban residence; growth accelerated after 1980 and later slowed with economic decline.
